Subject: Re: Interregional queue pressure — temporary p95/p99 uplift and mitigation plan

Hi Elena — thanks for the traces, that was helpful. Short summary from our side: we observed an interregional request imbalance starting ~08:30 PDT that caused queue pressure on a subset of GPU pools servicing northwest US regions. The routing layer briefly routed heavier-than-expected prefix traffic to a smaller pool which increased our tail latency while autoscaling caught up.

What we’ve done so far:
- Shifted routing to additional compatible pools in us-west-2 and us-east-1 to offload pressure (rolling, begun at 09:05 PDT).
- Temporarily increased continuous-batching window for low-priority prefix buckets to reduce scheduling overhead.
- Enabled a higher-priority KV cache pin for Lighthouse account prefixes to reduce cold-kv misses (short experiment).

Estimated impact: p95 improved within ~20 minutes; p99 reduction is in progress — we expect full p99 recovery by ~10:15 PDT, barring secondary effects.

Next steps we will take (tracked in the attached mitigation plan):
1) Complete routing redistribution and monitor for residual tail events (ETA 10:30 PDT).
2) Postmortem and kernel selection audit for the affected pools (assigned to runtime team).
3) Share a short incident summary + concrete mitigations within 24 hours.

I’ll keep this thread for customer updates and loop in the runtime on the postmortem. If you need an interim SLA credit escalation, let me know and I’ll put it through with Laura.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Hi all — internal follow-up and commitments:
- Root cause: preliminary points to routing decision that concentrated a high proportion of long-sequence requests on a smaller-than-expected pool when regional routing weights were rebalanced for capacity smoothing.
- Immediate mitigations taken: routing redistribution, targeted KV pinning for impacted prefixes, temporary batch-window tweak.
- Action items (owners & ETA):
  • Runtime: kernel selection audit and autoscaler tuning (Aditya — ETA 48 hours).
  • SRE: trace correlation and durable instrumentation (Jasmine — ETA 24 hours).
  • CS/AE: customer outreach + credit assessment (Ben — standing by; ETA 24 hours).

We’ll publish a short statuspage post summarizing the incident and mark it as resolved once p99 meets baseline for two consecutive 15-min windows. I’ll draft the postmortem doc and share a link here by EOD tomorrow.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
